records.studentRequestSummary: Asked for clarification on the difference between independent and dependent variables in the lamp setup.
records.bioVoiceResponseSummary: Clarified that lamp distance (proxy for relative light intensity) is changed (independent) and bubbles/min is measured (dependent).
records.exchangeSummary: Student request summary: Asked to clarify independent vs. dependent variables. | BioVoice response summary: Defined lamp distance as independent variable and bubble count per minute as dependent variable.

records.studentRequestSummary: Asked in Filipino whether the oxygen bubbles come from carbon dioxide or water.
records.bioVoiceResponseSummary: Provided a Filipino guiding question asking which molecule is split during the light-dependent stage.
records.exchangeSummary: Student request summary: Asked about source of oxygen bubbles in Hydrilla. | BioVoice response summary: Prompted student to consider water splitting (photolysis) in light reactions.

records.studentRequestSummary: Shared observation that bubbles increased closer to the lamp and asked why the rate levels off.
records.bioVoiceResponseSummary: Explained in Cebuano (with English science terms) how carbon dioxide or temperature becomes a limiting factor when light is plentiful.
records.exchangeSummary: Student request summary: Shared trial pattern and asked about rate plateau. | BioVoice response summary: Explained limiting factors (carbon dioxide, temperature) and asked student to restate in own words.

records.studentRequestSummary: Asked if the plant stops respiring when placed in the dark covered condition.
records.bioVoiceResponseSummary: Asked a guiding question about whether living plant cells still need ATP energy in darkness.
records.exchangeSummary: Student request summary: Asked about plant respiration in darkness. | BioVoice response summary: Guided student to recognize cellular respiration occurs day and night.

records.studentRequestSummary: Asked how to evaluate the claim that photosynthesis permanently removes all atmospheric carbon dioxide using the NOAA note.
records.bioVoiceResponseSummary: Clarified the distinction between photosynthetic carbon uptake and permanent storage, pointing to respiration, decomposition, and fire in the NOAA source.
records.exchangeSummary: Student request summary: Asked about evaluating permanent CO2 removal claim (LC 5). | BioVoice response summary: Referenced NOAA source on carbon return via respiration, decomposition, and fire.
